corrections.source_says: The procedure establishes that participants reviewed and rated one AI output per system per task, and leaves iterative co-writing to future work. Remove the unsupported assertions that participants did not prompt and that outputs were pre-generated; also qualify the pre-generated wording in eligibility.reason. No participant-produced creative output is reported as scored.

confirmed: The source is arXiv:2606.09587v1 [cs.HC], dated 8 Jun 2026, with 18 PDF pages; the title and authors Muhammad Haris Khan and Joel Wester match the form (PDF p. 1, title block and arXiv stamp).

The human study is a within-subjects evaluation of AI-generated responses, with no stated random assignment of AI assistance and no scored participant-produced creative output. Design other, core=no, and context_class=none are supported under the codebook (PDF pp. 7-9, Section 4.4).

N = 16 refers to the same people rating all systems, not separate groups; the Friedman analyses also use N = 16. No randomized count or participant exclusions are reported, and the analyzed sample is below 50 (PDF pp. 7-9, Section 4.4).
The demographic figures match: ages 22–48, mean age 28.1, 4 female and 12 male (PDF p. 9, Table 4).

Each participant reviewed four systems across three tasks, giving 12 response evaluations per participant, with 5-point ratings for originality, coherence, creativity, and usefulness (PDF p. 8, Section 4.4, Procedure).

Ratings were aggregated across three tasks per participant-system before Friedman tests. The reported p values concern omnibus differences across the four systems, not documented pairwise tests of SRT-Strong versus Baseline-Pure (PDF p. 8, Section 4.4, Analysis and Results).
Originality matches: SRT-Strong M = 3.40 versus Baseline-Pure M = 2.85 (+19%); chi2(3, N = 16) = 7.34, p = .062, W = .153 (PDF p. 9, Section 4.4, Originality, Coherence, and Transparency).
Usefulness matches: SRT-Strong M = 3.60 versus Baseline-Pure M = 3.10, described as 16% higher; chi2(3, N = 16) = 9.99, p = .019, Kendall’s W = .208 (PDF p. 8, Section 4.4, Perceived Usefulness).

Figure 6a labels usefulness means as Baseline-Pure 3.10, Baseline-HighTemp 2.77, SRT-Mild 2.94, and SRT-Strong 3.60; the caption specifies 95% confidence intervals (PDF p. 10, Figure 6a and caption; figure visually checked in memory).
Coherence matches: SRT-Strong M = 3.92, Mdn = 4.00 versus Baseline-Pure M = 3.48, Mdn = 3.50; chi2(3, N = 16) = 12.47, p = .006, Kendall’s W = .260 (PDF p. 8, Section 4.4, Perceived Coherence).
The one-line finding reproduces the reported means and p values correctly; its evidence concerns human ratings of AI output rather than creativity of assisted human output (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 4.4).

The computational counts match: 30 prompts, 10 per mode, five systems and 10 outputs per system/prompt yield the reported 1,500 outputs; the ablation reports 1,200 and the lambda sweep 750 outputs (PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 4.1-4.3).

The models and settings match: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct for SRT, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, baseline temperature 1.0/top-p 0.9, high temperature 1.5, beam count 5, and SRT lambda values 0.6 and 1.2 (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2; p. 5, Table 1 and Section 4.1).

The computational reported string matches Creative-mode diversity 0.49 versus 0.40 and Baseline-Beam 0.00, plus originality 0.50 versus 0.27, described as an 85% improvement. Diversity compares generated outputs from the same system and prompt, not different people (PDF p. 6, Section 4.1; p. 7, Figure 3, visually checked in memory).

Appendices A-D and their figures occupy pp. 11-17; Tables 5-8 are on p. 13, Tables 9-11 on p. 14, and Algorithm 1 on p. 18. These concern the computational experiments, with no additional human experiment or synthesis; leaving synthesis counts and pooled estimates empty is appropriate (PDF pp. 11-18).
summary: The paper reports a 16-person evaluation of AI-generated text, with no randomized study of people producing scored creative work, so core exclusion and context_class=none are supported. The recorded numbers and source version match the PDF; corrections concern unsupported population and prompting claims and the grouping of three computational experiments.
